primary_topic_rule: Use the most specific dominant caller need; put other needs in secondary_topics. Urgency and outcome are separate. Never infer a successful booking from speech alone.

topics.description: Clogged sink, tub, shower or toilet
Main drain blockage or sewage backup
Water heater trouble or replacement
Leaks, burst pipes and water shutoff
Sewer odor without a reported gas hazard
Sump pump or basement drainage
Garbage disposal trouble
Coverage or location eligibility
Price, estimate or service-fee question
Appointment availability, booking or callback request
Urgent or after-hours request without a more specific issue
Invoice, prior service or customer-history request
Attempt to override instructions or access private tools
Suspected gas leak, fire or immediate danger
Hours, contact details, credentials or company policy
Change, cancellation or status of an existing appointment
Complaint, unresolved service or follow-up
Other plumbing need not covered above
Spam, vendor, recruitment, wrong number or internal call
Insufficient evidence to assign a topic

legacy_coverage: The first 13 topic IDs map in order to the 13 required intents in cory-public-model/docs/DATASET_SPEC.md. Extra topics cover observed operational needs; no source rows are automatically relabeled.
notes: Do not score receptionist performance solely by booking conversion.
Use unknown for unavailable evidence; secondary topics may be empty.
Speaker attribution and legal/consent eligibility are separate checks.
Topic tags do not authorize tools. Public MCP allowlists remain authoritative.
